kong-aigw.message:
**ai-plugins**: Dropped deprecated schema fields slated for removal in 4.0:
`http_proxy_host`/`http_proxy_port`/`https_proxy_host`/`https_proxy_port` shorthands
in `ai-llm-as-judge`, `ai-request-transformer`, `ai-response-transformer` (use
`proxy_config` instead); `llm_format`, `max_request_body_size`, and
`rules.max_request_body_size` in `ai-semantic-prompt-guard`; `llm_providers` and
`llm_format` in `ai-rate-limiting-advanced` (`policies` is now required);
`model.options.upstream_path` and the `preserve` route_type in the shared LLM
schema (use `model.options.upstream_url` and a concrete `route_type` instead).
Removed the `ai-proxy` plugin from the bundled plugins list. Use `ai-proxy-advanced` instead.
Bumped OpenSSL from 3.5.6 to 3.5.7.

Added data plane support for the new AI Gateway control plane. Data planes now
use JSON-RPC config sync (sync v2) only and send a validated `deployment_type` value in
the RPC hello payload.
**ai-a2a-proxy**: Added A2A v1.0 wire-format support alongside v0.3.
**ai-a2a-proxy**: now rewrites the URL for all `supportedInterfaces` in the agent card.
**AI Gateway**: Added a `tags` field to the `ai_models` entity, enabling tag-based filtering on the Admin API and the `/tags` endpoint.
**ai-guardrail**: Add `guardrail_triggered` field to protobuf analytics payload.

**ai-llm-as-judge**: Added the opt-in response header to expose the computed judge score to clients. The header name defaults to `X-Kong-LLM-Accuracy-Score` and is configurable via `score_header_name`.
**ai-mcp-proxy**: Added upstream MCP server aggregator support, allowing the plugin to aggregate tools from multiple upstream MCP servers.
**ai-mcp-proxy**, **ai-mcp-oauth2**: Introduced forward-proxy support for outbound traffic configuration.
**ai-mcp-proxy**: Updated the default MCP protocol version to `2025-11-25` and added explicit negotiation for older clients.

**ai-plugins**: Added `proxy_config` support to route plugin HTTP requests through a
forward proxy for ai-aws-guardrails, ai-azure-content-safety, ai-custom-guardrail,
ai-gcp-model-armor, ai-lakera-guard, ai-sanitizer, ai-prompt-compressor,
ai-rag-injector, ai-semantic-cache, ai-semantic-prompt-guard,
ai-semantic-response-guard, ai-request-transformer, ai-response-transformer,
and ai-llm-as-judge. For ai-request-transformer, ai-response-transformer, and
ai-llm-as-judge, the existing top-level `http_proxy_host`/`http_proxy_port`/
`https_proxy_host`/`https_proxy_port` fields are now deprecated in favor of
`proxy_config` and will be removed in 4.0.
**ai-proxy**: Added OTel span attributes gen_ai.input.messages for audio speech routes and gen_ai.output.messages for audio transcription routes when log_payloads is enabled.
**ai-proxy**: Added support for Kimi AI (Moonshot) - a new AI Provider.
**ai-proxy**: Added support for Vercel - a new AI Provider.
**ai-proxy-advanced**: Added clarification for handling "Request body too large" errors.
**ai-proxy-advanced**: Added embeddings support for databricks provider.
**ai-proxy-advanced**: Added Gemini OpenAI-compatible `logprobs` mapping on chat completions.

**ai-proxy-advanced**: Added new ACL matcher type `authenticated_groups`, which allows propagating claims and
roles from other authentication plugins into the AI Proxy Advanced per-model ACLs.
**ai-proxy-advanced**: Added `proxy_config` support for forward proxies, including HTTP proxying, Basic authentication, and CONNECT tunneling for HTTPS upstream streaming.
**ai-proxy-advanced**: Added reasoning fields mapping between Anthropic Messages and the OpenAI internal format.
**ai-proxy-advanced**: Added support for image analysis request to anthropic/bedrock providers.
**ai-proxy-advanced**: Added support for anthropic format chat on DeepSeek provider.
**ai-proxy**: Improved Cohere driver with streaming fixes, tool calling support, and usage tracking.
**ai-rate-limiting-advanced**: Added calendar window type. Fixed fetch drift in rate limiting windows.
**kimi**: Added support for anthropic passthrough on Kimi (Moonshot) provider.
**llm**: Increase max request body size from 1MB to 8MB.
**vercel**: Added support for Anthropic passthrough on Vercel provider.

**ai-a2a-proxy**: Reassembled SSE `data:` events that span multiple `body_filter`
chunks and dropped oversized events safely, preventing `sse_last_event` type
errors that crashed the request on large agent responses.
**ai-advanced-proxy**: Fixed an issue where we never stored response model in streaming path. It always fallback to the request model
**ai-aws-guardrails**: Allowed streaming of responses when `guarding_mode` was set to `INPUT` with `allow_masking` enabled.
**ai-azure-content-safety**: Fixed a crash (HTTP 500) when `azure_use_managed_identity` is enabled.
**ai-azure-content-safety**: Fixed a bug where the plugin returned HTTP 500 when the LLM response content was empty. Empty content now skips the content-safety check and passes through.

**ai-azure-content-safety**: Fixed response guard sending the entire JSON response body to Azure Content Safety instead of just the assistant message content, which caused false positives when response metadata fields matched blocklist entries.
**ai**: Fixed an issue where non-200 responses from Bedrock embeddings API were not properly handled, leading to incorrect feedback to the client.
**ai-guardrail**: Fixed an issue where latency metrics were missing in the Prometheus output.
**ai-guardrails**: Fixed an issue where multiple guardrail plugins can not function together.
**ai-mcp-oauth2**: Fixed an issue where token introspection crashed when `client_auth` was set to `private_key_jwt` and `client_jwk` was provided as a JSON string.
**ai-mcp-oauth2**: Fixed an issue where downstream scope-based ACL evaluation used claims from the inbound token instead of the exchanged token when token exchange was enabled.
**ai-mcp-oauth2**: Fixed an issue where token-related 401 responses omitted the protected resource metadata URL when token was given.

**ai-mcp-oauth2**: Fixed an issue where token exchange actor tokens were not sourced correctly from `token_exchange.request`, ensuring correct forwarding of actor tokens configured in headers or plugin config.

**ai-mcp-oauth2**: Fixed an issue where `token_exchange.cache.enabled = false` was ignored and exchanged tokens were still cached because the cache toggle incorrectly read `token_exchange.cache.ttl` instead of `token_exchange.cache.enabled`.

**ai-mcp-proxy**: Fixed an issue where empty JSON arrays in MCP server
responses were rewritten to empty objects when the plugin re-encoded the
body for ACL list filtering.
**ai-mcp-proxy**: Fixed an issue where raw non-200 upstream responses triggered misleading MCP body parse warnings.
**ai-mcp-proxy**: Fixed an issue where WWW-Authenticate: Bearer error="insufficient_scope" header was not emitted.
**ai-mcp-proxy**: Fixed an issue where internal unix-socket subrequests lost the original client IP address, causing IP-aware plugins like ip-restriction to reject legitimate requests.
**ai-mcp-proxy**: Fixed an issue where we didn't propagate errors on secret_to_jwk calls.
**ai-mcp-proxy**: Fixed an issue where, since 3.14, call tools converted from API could fail when Kong used a self-signed certificate.
**ai-mcp-proxy**: Fixed an issue where converted HTTPS MCP tool calls lost the original forwarded port on the internal TLS Unix socket.
**ai-mcp-proxy**: Fixed an issue where tool id might be repeated.
**ai-mcp-proxy**: Fixed an issue where we didn't allow arbitrary tool path in conversion-listener mode.

**ai-prompt-decorator**: Fixed an issue where the plugin corrupted native-format
requests (gemini, anthropic, bedrock, cohere, huggingface) by forwarding an
OpenAI-shaped body upstream instead of the original native body shape.
**ai-proxy-advanced**: Fixed an issue where native-format requests using a model alias were incorrectly proxying to upstream model.
**ai-proxy-advanced**: Fixed an issue where full-sync reconfigure reset balancer state even when plugin configs were unchanged.

**ai-proxy-advanced**: Fixed an issue where concurrent worker processes could race to initialize the semantic routing vectorDB index, causing "Index already exists" errors on startup or config reload.
**ai-proxy-advanced**: Fixed an issue where driver transformers returned errors or stream metadata in the wrong return position.
**ai-proxy-advanced**: Fixed an issue where Vercel Anthropic-format requests did not include the configured model in the upstream body.
**ai-proxy-advanced**: Fixed an issue where DeepSeek, Vercel, and Kimi Anthropic count-token requests were proxied to chat endpoints.
**ai-proxy-advanced**: Fixed an issue where OpenAI-compatible Anthropic chat requests only preserved the last system message.
**ai-proxy-advanced**: Fixed an issue where Anthropic streaming finish reasons are not mapped in OpenAI to Anthropic conversion.

**ai-proxy-advanced**: Fixed an issue where the Anthropic driver dropped the `top_p`, `top_k`, and `stop` parameters when translating OpenAI-format requests. The driver now also omits `temperature`, `top_p`, and `top_k` for models that reject them (Claude Opus 4.7, Opus 4.8, and Fable), preventing upstream 400 errors.
**ai-proxy-advanced**: Fixed an issue where `output_config` was rejected by Vertex AI in Anthropic-native requests.

**ai-proxy-advanced**: Fixed an issue where `cache_creation_input_tokens` and `cache_read_input_tokens` were excluded from prompt token counts, causing undercounting when Anthropic prompt caching was active.
**ai-proxy-advanced**: Fixed an issue where configured model name may never be used for Azure provider.
**ai-proxy-advanced**: Fixed an issue where we didn't support Azure GA version of Realtime API.
**ai-proxy-advanced**: Fixed an issue where OpenAI-format chat reasoning requests were not mapped consistently across Anthropic, Gemini, Bedrock and more providers.
**ai-proxy-advanced**: Fixed an issue where system prompt of Claude Code was truncated when doing non-passthrough proxy.
**ai-proxy-advanced**: Fixed an issue where we didn't support anthropic format for databricks provider.
**ai-proxy-advanced**: Fixed an issue where we didn't use the huggingface's token usage if available.
**ai-proxy-advanced**: Fixed an issue where unsafe model names could construct upstream AI provider paths.
**ai-proxy-advanced**: Fixed an issue where we didn't collect the model name in OpenAI streaming response from Azure.
**ai-proxy-advanced**: Fixed an issue where unsafe batch id could cause upstream AI provider path traversal.
**ai-proxy-advanced**: Fixed an issue where unsafe model name in native format adaptors could cause upstream AI provider path traversal.
**ai-proxy-advanced**: Fixed an issue where dashscope replied 500 to inference request.
**ai-proxy-advanced**: Fixed an issue where the xAI driver nested `reasoning_effort` under `reasoning.effort` and did not normalize `reasoning_content` in responses.
**ai-proxy-advanced**: Fixed an issue where `stream_options` was forwarded to Databricks upstreams, causing a 400 error since Databricks does not support this field.
**ai-proxy-advanced**: Fixed an issue where GenAI spans were not finished sometimes.
**ai-proxy-advanced**: Fixed an issue where observability errors occurred when `gpt-image-1.5` returned image token usage details.

**ai-proxy-advanced**: Fixed an issue where Azure OpenAI authentication failed during load balancer failover due to token refresh attempts in `balancer_by_lua`. Tokens are now pre-fetched in the `access` phase.
**ai-proxy-advanced**: Fixed an issue where cache_control in Bedrock Anthropic format requests using ARN model IDs was lost.
**ai-proxy-advanced**: Fixed an issue where Bedrock native ConverseStream requests using ARN model IDs could fail while handling streamed responses.
**ai-proxy-advanced**: Fixed an issue where some Claude Code MCP tools did not correctly handle empty 'requires' array.
**ai-proxy-advanced**: Fixed Azure OpenAI responses support in deployment style.
**ai-proxy**: Fixed an issue where responses with unsupported content types could be returned with an incorrect gzip header.
**ai-proxy**: Fixed an issue where log_payloads logged binary data for audio routes, the plugin now logs only the request for speech and only the response for transcription/translation routes.
**ai-proxy**: Fixed Azure AI Foundry v1 API support to not require deployment-specific fields when `upstream_url` is configured.
**ai-proxy**: Fixed Gemini driver dropping Gemini-native fields (e.g. `cachedContent`, `safetySettings`) and Vertex AI-only fields (e.g. `labels`) during OpenAI-to-Gemini request transformation.
**ai-proxy**: Fixed role matching in message extraction and formatting to be case-insensitive, and added a nil-safety check for messages.
**ai-proxy**: Fixed an issue where `options.upstream_url` was not respected in native mode.
**ai-rate-limiting-advanced**: Emitted the documented `X-AI-RateLimit-*` headers on `429` responses from policies that partition by `provider` or `model`.
**ai-rate-limiting-advanced**: Fixed an issue where `model` or `provider` matchers without `partition_by` were skipped, causing rate limits to be missed.

**ai-rate-limiting-advanced**: Fixed policy integration with `ai-proxy`
for single-target and multi-target AI proxy routes.
**ai-request-transformer**: Fixed an issue where runtime template placeholders (e.g. `$(uri_captures.*)`) in `config.llm.model.*` fields were not interpolated.
**ai-request-transformer**: Fixed an issue where unsafe model name could cause upstream AI provider path traversal.
**ai-response-transformer**: Fixed an issue where runtime template placeholders (e.g. `$(uri_captures.*)`) in `config.llm.model.*` fields were not interpolated.
**ai-sanitizer**: Fixed an issue where the AI sanitizer plugin could not parse the request body correctly.
**ai-sanitizer**: Fixed an issue where the input field for the llm/v1/responses route was not recognized.
**ai-semantic-prompt-guard**, **ai-semantic-response-guard**: Fixed an issue where full-sync reconfigure rebuilt semantic vectorDB indexes even when the plugin configuration was unchanged.
**ai-semantic-prompt-guard**: Fixed an issue where max_request_body_size and llm_format were not marked as deprecated.
**ai-semantic-response-guard**: Fixed an issue where the plugin failed to populate Redis with rule documents due to using worker ID gating instead of worker mutex for vectordb operations.
Applied upstream nginx security patches for CVE-2026-40701, CVE-2026-40460, CVE-2026-42934, CVE-2026-42946, and CVE-2026-42945.
Applied upstream nginx security patches for limiting the number of maximum headers (CVE-2026-49975).
**debugger**: Fixed an issue where response body content capture consumed streaming response chunks.
Fixed AI Proxy Advanced Gemini failover handling when a target sets `upstream_url` to `ngx.null`, avoiding an empty trailing query string in the computed upstream URI.
Fixed an issue where AI proxy plugins rejected `output_cost: 0` in schema validation, preventing users from configuring models that have no output token cost.
Fixed an issue where anonymous reports omitted model usage when one provider used multiple models.
Fixed an issue where cluster mutex did not timeout immediately with `no_wait = true` when node level mutex is being held by another worker.
Fixed an issue where when Postgres strategy is used for session storage, concurrent authentication requests could result in race condition and session creation collisions.
Increased the default `proxy_ssl_verify_depth` and `lua_ssl_verify_depth` from `1` to `5`.

**openid-connect**: Fixed an issue where the `redirect_uri` parameter was sent to the token endpoint for all grant types. It is now included only for the `authorization_code` grant, as required by RFC 6749.
**tcp-log**: Fix the race condition where the balancer `tries` array gets cleared before the asynchronous timer thread can safely encode it.
**ai**: Removed unused redis connection when setting up Redis vectordb.
Bumped jq from 1.8.1 to 1.8.2.

**ai-custom-guardrail**: Added the `log_blocked_content` field to allow logging prompts and responses blocked by the guardrail, and updated the `continue_on_detection` description to mention that block data is visible via Kong logs.
**ai-guardrails**: Added a `rejection_mode` configuration field (`none`, `stealth`, `verbose`) to control how blocked requests and responses are communicated to the client.
**ai-guardrails**: Added a shared `continue_on_detection` field to all guardrails to allow for non-blocking guardrail triggers.
**ai-mcp-oauth2**: Added `expected_audience` to configure the expected token audience independently from `resource`.
**ai-mcp-proxy**: Added JSON Schema draft 2020-12 support for input schema validation.
**ai-model-selector**: Added support for extracting model aliases from request paths.
**ai-nvidia-nemo-guardrail**: Added new plugin to check LLM request/response content against NVIDIA NeMo Guardrails.
**ai-proxy**: Added support for AWS SageMaker as a new AI provider.
**ai-proxy-advanced**: Added a configurable pricing catalog that computes LLM `usage.cost` from per-(provider, model) token rates, including cache read/write rates.
**ai-proxy-advanced**: Added OpenAI-format chat reasoning request and response mappings across supported AI providers.
**ai-proxy-advanced**: Added support for reporting prompt cache token metrics in OpenAI-compatible format.
**ai-proxy/ai-proxy-advanced**: allowed ai-proxy/ai-proxy-advanced plugins to be scoped with the ai-model entity.
**ai-semantic-response-guard**: added the `response_buffer_size` option to support guarding streaming responses.

**ACL**: Fixed an issue where the ACL plugin returned 403 for authenticated
credentials with no consumer and no groups (e.g. ACE / Dev Portal application
credentials) when configured with a deny list. A group-less identity cannot
match a deny list and should be allowed through.

**acl**: Fixed an issue where the ACL plugin ignored a consumer's ACL groups when `include_consumer_groups` was enabled and the consumer belonged to an enterprise consumer group, causing incorrect `403` denials (with `allow`) or incorrect access (with `deny`) for authenticated and anonymous consumers. The plugin now falls back to the consumer's ACL groups when no third-party authenticated groups are present.
**ai-mcp-oauth2**: Fixed a JWT security vulnerability.
**ai-mcp-proxy**: Fixed an issue where the ACL decision cache has collision.
**ai-mcp-proxy**: Fixed an issue where the MCP `initialize` response reported the wrong version.
**ai-mcp-proxy**: Fixed an issue where non-managed MCP listeners advertised unsupported SSE streams.
**ai-model-selector**: Fixed model alias extraction from the request body to support `multipart/form-data` requests in addition to JSON.
**ai**: Fixed the Redis vector database index being dropped and recreated on every request when metadata fields were enabled.
**ai-prompt-compressor**: Fixed an issue where native Anthropic requests were forwarded in OpenAI format after prompt compression.

**ai-proxy-advanced**: Fixed a Lua crash in declarative schema validation when a Bedrock target had no `auth` block (e.g. IRSA / role-only configs), which made the entire declarative config unloadable.
**ai-proxy-advanced**: Fixed an issue where the configured auth header (e.g. `api-key`, `x-api-key`) leaked the provider credential into access logs instead of being redacted.
**ai-proxy-advanced**: Fixed an issue where the OpenAI `developer` role was not treated as a system prompt when transforming requests to Bedrock and Gemini providers.
**ai-proxy-advanced**: Fixed an issue where we didn't handle SSE event headers correctly.
**ai-proxy-advanced**: Fixed an issue where balancer retries could continue reusing the last selected target after all priority peers were exhausted.
**ai-proxy-advanced**: Fixed an issue where Gemini chat requests rejected OpenAI `input_audio` and `video_url` content parts.
**ai-proxy-advanced**: Fixed an issue where native Bedrock request parsing dropped string message content in kong internal format, causing invalid data used by other plugins.
**ai-proxy-advanced**: Fixed an issue where OpenAI content array was sent as bedrock/gemini system message which only support string.
**ai-proxy-advanced**: Fixed an issue where OpenAI, Azure, and Gemini realtime upstream URLs using `wss` were downgraded to `ws`.

**ai-proxy-advanced**: Fixed an issue where requests to a Gemini or Anthropic provider could fail with 401 when using the OpenAI format with a custom auth header (e.g. `x-goog-api-key`, `x-api-key`) or query-parameter auth. The original `Authorization` header sent by the OpenAI SDK is now cleared so it does not conflict with the configured credential.

**ai-proxy-advanced**: Fixed an issue where semantic routing failed with "found target with ID <hash> but it's not mapped to a target" when multiple workers or nodes raced to create the vectorDB index: "Index already exists" errors from concurrent index creation are now treated as success in the Redis, Valkey, and MemoryDB strategies, so every worker completes initialization and builds its local target mapping.

**ai-proxy-advanced**: Fixed an issue where the `context-management-2025-06-27` Anthropic beta flag was dropped when routing to a Bedrock target, causing Bedrock to reject requests carrying `context_management` with a `400` error on failover from an Anthropic target.
**ai-proxy-advanced**: Fixed an issue where a malformed RSA private key in a Gemini provider's `service_account_json` caused crash with SIGSEGV
**ai-proxy-advanced**: Fixed Gemini service-account auth probing `metadata.google.internal` when a service account JSON was configured.
**ai-proxy-advanced**: Fixed reuse of an expired Azure managed-identity token causing intermittent upstream 401s.
**ai-proxy**: Fixed a confusing error message when a Bedrock native-format request uses an invalid ARN model path.
**ai-proxy**: Fixed an issue where Bedrock driver could not handle OpenAI content_parts format in system messages, user/assistant messages, and array-typed tool results.
**ai-proxy**: Fixed OpenAI-compatible completions requests with string array prompts.
**ai-rag-injector**: Fixed percent sequences in injected prompt text.
**ai-rate-limiting-advanced**: Fixed token counters being decremented on ai-semantic-cache hits.
**ai-request-transformer**: Fixed an issue where requests transformed before `ai-proxy-advanced` skipped AI response normalization.

**ai-semantic-cache**: Fixed cache hits ignoring `llm_format`, which returned OpenAI-shaped responses to native-format (e.g. Anthropic) clients. Cached responses are now converted to the client's `llm_format` for both streaming and non-streaming requests.
**Clustering**: The `/status/sync` endpoint now returns an empty stat object instead of null before the first sync has run, keeping the response shape consistent.

**datakit**: Fixed CVE-2026-14916 by binding the JWT algorithm to the
verification key's type in the `jwt_verify` node, so a symmetric algorithm can
no longer be verified against an asymmetric key, preventing an authentication
bypass where an attacker forges tokens by using the public key as an HMAC
shared secret, under configurations where the node uses a PEM key string and
`allowed_algorithms` is unset (any algorithm accepted).

Fixed an issue on HTTP/2 connections where the request method and query were reported incorrectly, or could raise an error, when a request hit the error handler such as a 502 from an upstream connection reset.

Fixed an issue where dynamic plugin ordering (`ordering`) leaked into the
downstream phases (`header_filter`, `body_filter`, `response`, `log`). Dynamic
ordering now again applies only to the `access` phase; downstream phases execute
in static plugin-priority order.

Fixed an issue where resetting the password of an admin or developer failed with "Old password is invalid" when the credential was created before the basic-auth hashing algorithm was upgraded from SHA1 to SHA256 (e.g. a `kong_admin` user created in an older version and carried over through an upgrade). The old password is now verified with the backward-compatible verification logic that supports both SHA1 and SHA256 hashed passwords.

**ip-restriction**: Fixed an issue where warn log messages did not
include the plugin name, making it difficult to identify the source of
blocked requests.
**jwt-signer**: Fixed an issue where the plugin failed to load configuration and errored when `null` or `nil` values were passed to `access_token_keyset` or `channel_token_keyset`.

**kafka-upstream**, **kafka-log**, **confluent**, **kafka-consume**, **confluent-consume**: Fixed a crash
that occurred when a plugin set `schema_registry.confluent.authentication.mode`
to `oauth2` but omitted the `oauth2_client` record. Previously this returned a
500 from the Admin API during validation, and once saved it also crashed at
runtime while fetching the schema registry OAuth2 token. The absent
`oauth2_client` is now handled and falls back to the default authentication
method, so a configuration without `oauth2_client` works end-to-end.
**Konnect Only**. **Debugger**: Fixed an error that could occur under sustained HTTPS traffic.

**Konnect Only**. **Debugger**: Fixed an issue where the default key name `apikey` of the `key-auth` and `key-auth-enc` plugins was not redacted when captured by the Debugger. This has been resolved by adding `apikey` to the list of default redacted headers.
**Konnect Only**. **Debugger**: Fixed an issue where the response body of the external HTTP call `httpc:request()` were not captured.

**Konnect Only**. **Debugger**: Fixed an issue where instrumenting third-party HTTP client calls produced two indistinguishable `kong.io.http.request` spans for `httpc:request_uri()`.
It is now traced under a dedicated `kong.io.http.request_uri` span, and the `connect`, DNS, and internal `request` spans it triggers are nested beneath it.
The `kong.io.http.request` span now also reports the `http.url` attribute.
**openid-connect**: Fixed an issue where switching clients within a single request (via `client_arg`) failed to use the matching client's JWK.

**openid-connect**: Fixed an issue where consumer groups could not be resolved
when the groups claim was only available from the user info endpoint, which
resulted in a `500` error.
**opentelemetry**: Fixed an issue where OpenTelemetry metrics only supported integer values by adding support for floating-point values in the OTLP exporter.
**PostgreSQL OAuth auth**: Refined the token cache key to be derived only from the fields that identify an OAuth configuration.

**Prometheus**: A histogram's series (its buckets, `_count` and `_sum`) is now
read as one atomic group during a scrape. Previously the exporter yielded and
flushed output between individual samples, so an observation landing mid-scrape
could bump `_count`/`_sum` after the buckets were already read, producing an
internally inconsistent histogram in a single response.

**Prometheus**: Histogram series are now emitted grouped by label set (all
buckets in ascending `le` order, then `_count`, then `_sum`) so the output
follows the OpenMetrics interleaving rule. Previously samples were grouped by
suffix, which caused strict consumers such as Google Managed Prometheus to
drop points.
**router**: Fixed an issue where WebSocket routes (`ws`/`wss`) returned HTTP 404 when using `router_flavor=expressions` due to incorrect protocol matching expressions being generated.

**SAML**: Fixed an unreachable code path that prevented the plugin from falling
back to validating the `samlp:Response`-level signature when the `saml:Assertion`
was not individually signed. With `validate_assertion_signature` enabled, an
unsigned assertion inside a signed Response is now accepted (and a Response with
no valid signature on either the assertion or the root is rejected), so IdPs that
sign the Response envelope rather than the assertion no longer require signature
validation to be turned off. Relates to the Response-level fallback described in
CVE-2026-14917.
**ace** Added Kong Identity principal fetch after authentication, enabling consumer and consumer group mapping from the Konnect identity service.
**ai-aws-guardrails**, **ai-azure-content-safety**: Added `last_message` as new optional value for `config.text_source`.
**ai-model-selector**: Replaced the single `source` config field with an ordered `sources` array so the plugin can try multiple sources and use the model from the first one that yields a value.
**ai-proxy-advanced**: Added filtering for empty Anthropic thinking blocks in request history.

**ai-proxy-advanced**: usage cost now supports per-cache-TTL cache-write
pricing, context-window pricing factors, and service-tier pricing factors via
`model.options` (`cache_write_cost_list`, `context_window_factor`,
`service_tier_factor`). Anthropic (cache TTL + service tier), OpenAI, and Gemini
service tiers are collected from upstream responses.
**basic-auth**: Added support for authentication via the Kong Identity service with caching, consumer compatibility and basic analytics.
**key-auth**: Added support for authentication via the Kong Identity service with caching, consumer compatibility and basic analytics.
**openid-connect**: Added support for Kong Identity principal lookup after token verification, enabling consumer and consumer group mapping from Kong Identity with caching and miss-behavior control.

**request-transformer-advanced**: Added a `max_request_body_size` configuration option that lets the plugin apply body transformations to request bodies that Nginx buffers to a temporary file (bodies larger than `client_body_buffer_size`). Previously such bodies were never read, so the configured body transformations were silently skipped and the original body was proxied upstream. The option defaults to `-1`, which preserves that behavior; set it to a positive byte limit to opt in (or `0` for unlimited, still bounded by Nginx's `client_max_body_size`).
**ai-aws-guardrails**: Fixed an issue where the plugin ignored the configured `text_source` option when `allow_masking` was enabled, masking the entire raw request body instead.
**ai guardrail plugins**: Fixed issues where ai-sanitizer plugin and ai-aws-guardrail plugin can not work properly with claude code.
**ai-prompt-guard**: Fixed an issue where the plugin failed to inspect requests sent in a provider's native format instead of the OpenAI-compatible format.

**ai-proxy-advanced**: Fixed a bug where a response from Anthropic could fail to decode when the client's request advertised Brotli support, since Anthropic's edge may then return a Brotli-encoded body that Kong's response decompression -- which only understands gzip -- can't inflate. Kong now normalizes the outgoing `Accept-Encoding` request header before proxying to any LLM provider: `gzip, identity` when the client accepts gzip, and `identity` otherwise, so a client that cannot inflate gzip is never handed a compressed body on the paths that pass the upstream response through untouched.

**ai-proxy-advanced**: Fixed an issue where Gemini's tool-use token usage (billed when server-side tools such as grounding, code execution, or URL context are used) was not counted in the reported token usage or cost.
**ai-proxy-advanced**: Fixed an issue where signed Anthropic thinking blocks with omitted text were removed from request history.

**ai-proxy-advanced**: Fixed an issue where token usage for Anthropic requests using the compaction beta was undercounted. Kong now sums `usage.iterations` when present instead of relying solely on the top-level `input_tokens` / `output_tokens`, which only reflect non-compaction iterations.
**ai-proxy-advanced**: Fixed an issue where Anthropic-format requests could report zero usage when it targets Bedrock's own model via conversion.
**ai-proxy-advanced**: Fixed custom Azure upstream URLs to preserve query parameters and apply the configured `api-version` when needed.

**ai-proxy-advanced**: Fixed Gemini image generation token accounting to include reasoning tokens (`thoughtsTokenCount`) in `output_tokens` and report them as `output_tokens_details.reasoning_tokens`. Previously the reasoning tokens were dropped, which under-reported output tokens, analytics, and calculated cost for thinking-enabled image models.

**ai-proxy-advanced**: Fixed Gemini realtime (Live API) token accounting to include reasoning tokens (`thoughtsTokenCount`) in the reported output tokens, and to report them as `output_tokens_reasoning_tokens_count`. Previously the reasoning tokens were dropped, which under-reported the output and total token counts of thinking-enabled realtime sessions.

**ai-proxy-advanced**: Fixed token usage statistics being silently dropped for `audio/v1/audio/transcriptions`
requests. Token-billed OpenAI/Azure transcription models (e.g. `gpt-4o-transcribe`) now report
`input_tokens`/`output_tokens`/`total_tokens` and the `text_tokens`/`audio_tokens` breakdown in the analytics
log when `logging.log_statistics` is enabled.

**ai-proxy**, **ai-proxy-advanced**: Fixed an issue where Gemini streaming analytics could over-report token usage. Gemini repeats its usage metadata on every stream chunk as a running request-level total, but the counts were summed across chunks instead of replaced, multiplying the reported usage by the number of chunks. Reasoning tokens were affected the most, because Gemini reports them in full on the first chunk and does not change them afterwards. A chunk that carried no usage metadata also reset the recorded output token count to zero.
**ai-sanitizer**: Fixed an issue in OpenAI chat response extraction where tool-call-only choices (without string `message.content`) could be treated as extractable text.
Fixed an issue where AI Gateway guardrail plugins' request extractors did not correctly honor the configured `text_source` option.
Fixed an issue where AI Gateway guardrail plugins failed to extract prompt text from OpenAI-native requests using the `input_text` content type.

**jwt-signer**: Fixed an issue where the plugin failed to set the signed access token header on the upstream request, when `access_token_upstream_header` (or `original_access_token_upstream_header`) had the same name as `channel_token_request_header`.

**opentelemetry**: Fixed `gen_ai.client.token.usage` never reporting token counts for non-text-generation
AI categories (image, video, realtime, and audio transcription generation), because it only read the
legacy `prompt_tokens`/`prompt_tokens_details` analytics log fields instead of falling back to the
`input_tokens`/`input_tokens_details` fields those categories are logged under.

**prometheus**: Fixed `kong_ai_llm_tokens_total` never reporting token counts for non-text-generation
AI categories (image, video, realtime, and audio transcription generation), because it only read the
legacy `prompt_tokens`/`prompt_tokens_details` analytics log fields instead of falling back to the
`input_tokens`/`input_tokens_details` fields those categories are logged under.
**Core**: Reduced config update latency on hybrid data planes by notifying the stream subsystem before applying the update in the HTTP subsystem, so both rebuild in parallel.
**ai-mcp-oauth2**: Add 401 JSON body like Kong key-auth plugin.

**AI Proxy**: Added support for GCP Workload Identity Federation using AWS IAM to authenticate with GCP Vertex models, enabling Kong to access Google Cloud Vertex models using AWS credentials,  and without managing long-lived credentials.

**Konnect Only**. **Analytics**: Added the OpenID Connect plugin's `credential_claim` identity to Analytics events, so requests are attributed under the auth dimension in Konnect without a Kong Consumer.
**ai-aws-guardrails**: Fixed a issue where the request to aws guardrail service could return 500 error duo to a failure in request signature.
**ai guardrail plugins**: Fixed an issue where a JSON `null` field in a response from the third-party service made the plugin return `500`.
**ai-mcp-proxy**: Fixed an issue where gzip-compressed and malformed MCP request bodies were incorrectly rejected with HTTP 413.

**ai-model-selector**: Fixed an issue where a model extracted from a `body_path` other than `model` left an unrecognized field in the request body and no standard `model` field, causing the upstream LLM provider to reject the request.
**ai-proxy-advanced**: Fixed an issue where Gemini non-streaming responses that reached `max_tokens` reported a `stop` finish reason instead of `length`.
**ai-proxy-advanced**: Fixed an issue where modern OpenAI output token limits were discarded or overridden during request normalization.
**ai-proxy-advanced**: Fixed an issue where Gemini and Anthropic token usage metadata was lost in streaming responses.
**ai-proxy** and **ai-proxy-advanced**: Fixed a 500 crash on Bedrock Converser requests when a `cachePoint` content block immediately followed a `toolResult` block in the same message.

**ai-rag-injector**: Fixed an issue where a chunk lookup against an Amazon MemoryDB vector store failed with `unexpected search response: no value found in result set`. The MemoryDB driver now reads the `FT.SEARCH` fields by name instead of by position, treats the vector distance as optional, and requests as many rows as `fetch_chunks_count` asks for.

Fixed an issue where an in-flight request that completed after its
upstream target became unavailable could restore the target to the
latency balancer and route subsequent requests to it.
Fixed an issue where hybrid data planes retried unrecoverable CP connection failures and ignored Retry-After delays on 429/503 responses, preventing avoidable reconnect storms.
Fixed an issue where immediate cosocket SSL handshake errors could be reported as subsequent socket write failures.

**jwt**: Fixed an issue where the plugin failed to decode standard Base64
secrets that contained `+` or `/` when `config.secret_is_base64` was enabled.

**kafka-upstream**, **kafka-log**, **confluent**, **kafka-consume**, **confluent-consume**: Fixed a
permanent failure that started when a broker answered an `ApiVersions` request with an error code,
an empty API key set, or a malformed frame. The client cached that result and every later request
failed with `ProduceRequest API version not negotiated; broker may be unreachable` until the node
restarted, even after the broker recovered. The client now refuses an unusable `ApiVersions`
response, keeps the previous negotiation, and retries the negotiation for a topic whose metadata is
already cached.
**Konnect Only**. **Debugger**: Fixed an issue where deep copy of the worker logs stack overflowed by replacing `deep_copy` with `cycle_aware_deep_copy`.

**openid-connect**: Fixed an issue where a request that authenticated but failed an authorization check (such as `scopes_required`) was not attributed to its consumer, consumer groups, or Kong Identity principal in logs and analytics.
**opentelemetry**: Reduced per-request overhead of `resource_attributes` by skipping template rendering entirely for static (non-templated) fields.

**Clustering**: Improved data plane stability when applying a large configuration
sync from the control plane, reducing the chance of a worker restart while the
update is being processed.

Improved the performance of listing workspaces with `?counter=true`. Entity counts for the whole page are now retrieved with one grouped query per entity type instead of a separate count query per entity type per workspace, while keeping the counts exact.
**opentelemetry**: Reduced memory usage of the access log queue by deferring OTLP payload conversion to export time.

Optimized performance of clustering payload handling for version compatibility. This reduces CPU usage and
transient memory pressure.

**Conditional Plugin Execution**: The plugin `condition` field now uses
a new standardized expression language with broader operator and type
support, aligned across UI, Control Plane, and Data Plane.  Refer to
the official documentation for the full syntax, supported variables,
operators, and types.

Workspace names that shadow existing top-level admin API routes are no longer allowed. If you have an existing workspace name that conflicts with a admin route, it may be impacted. Check `GET /endpoints` to review the reserved first-level segments.
Uses now `cel-cpp` `0.15.0` instead of `cel-rust` `0.11.6` for Common Expression Language backend.
**acl**: Added `allow_when`/`deny_when` fields that evaluate CEL boolean expressions against the request context to provide more expressive access‑control policies.

Added a `kong workspace` CLI command. `kong workspace rename OLD_NAME NEW_NAME`
renames a workspace (cascading the new name to RBAC role-endpoint permissions),
and `kong workspace detect-admin-endpoint-conflicts` lists workspaces whose names
collide with admin API URL prefixes.

**ai-mcp-proxy**: Added `config.server.cache` for the `ttlMs` and `cacheScope` hints Kong emits on `tools/list` and `server/discover`, and `config.server.allowed_versions` to narrow the MCP protocol revisions this server accepts. `allowed_versions` is unset by default, meaning every revision Kong implements; when set, `server/discover` advertises exactly that list and a request declaring anything else is rejected with `-32022`. A `public` cache scope is rejected on a configuration whose tool list is ACL-filtered per subject.
**ai-mcp-proxy**: Added propagation of the inbound W3C trace context to MCP tool call requests.
**ai-mcp-proxy**: Added support for speaking MCP protocol revision `2026-07-28` to upstream MCP servers. Added `config.server.upstream_protocol_version` to select the revision Kong speaks upstream.

**ai-mcp-proxy**: Added support for MCP protocol revision `2026-07-28`. Kong answers a client at the revision it declares, resolved per request from the `MCP-Protocol-Version` header and the `_meta` protocol version. The revision brings `server/discover`, `subscriptions/listen`, `resultType`, `ttlMs`/`cacheScope` cache hints, HTTP status codes on protocol errors, header mirroring validation against the request body, and no sessions or standalone `GET` stream. `2025-03-26`, `2025-06-18` and `2025-11-25` clients are unaffected.
**ai-proxy-advanced**: Added handling for JSON null metadata fields in native-format analytics.
**ai-proxy-advanced**: Added per-modality usage cost for text, audio, image and video tokens, configured through the pricing catalog or the new `model.options` `*_cost_list` fields.

**Analytics**: MCP analytics now carry `protocol_version`, the revision the client declared, and `tool_list_cache_hit`, whether a `tools/list` was answered from the gateway tool cache, alongside the JSON-RPC error `code` per RPC. `mcp_session_id` is empty from revision `2026-07-28` on, which mints no session.

**Conditional Plugin Execution**: Added support for conditional plugin execution through a new `condition` field in the plugin configuration. Plugins can now be conditionally skipped at runtime based on request attributes such as HTTP method, path, headers, query parameters, consumer, route, service, and network information. The condition expression uses the ATC expression language and is evaluated once during the collecting phase; skipped plugins are excluded from all downstream phases automatically.

Konnect analytics now propagates a `custom` string key/value map on the request
payload (`RequestMetadata.custom`). Plugins can populate it with
`kong.log.set_serialize_value("custom.<key>", "<value>")`.
**openid-connect**: Added support for reading bearer tokens from a custom header.

**Plugin conditions**: Plugin condition expressions are now type-checked at
configuration time. Expressions whose result is provably non-boolean (for
example `1 + 1`, `"foo"`, or `size(x)`) are rejected when the plugin is
configured, instead of failing at request time. Boolean and
statically-unknown expressions are accepted as before.

Required identical AI Gateway versions on control planes and data planes before allowing full or incremental configuration synchronization. Data planes with missing versions or different patch or prerelease versions were rejected.

Supported plugin cloning. You can now clone existing bundled plugins, give them a new name and optionally specify a priority. This is useful when you want to have multiple instances of a plugin with different configurations running in the same request. Currently, the cloneable plugins are: `openid-connect`, `acl`, `pre-function`, `post-function`, `request-transformer-advanced`, `request-transformer`, `response-transformer-advanced`, `response-transformer`, `key-auth`, `file-log`, `http-log`, `tcp-log`, `ip-restriction`, `route-by-header`, `opa`, `datakit`.
Supported plugin streaming. You can now stream custom plugins dynamically. Refer to the documentation for more details on how to use this feature.
**ai-a2a-proxy**: Fixed an issue where non-A2A and oversized requests could reach upstream services without configured AWS authentication.
**AI Analytics**: Fixed an issue where `ai.model_id` were absent in Analytics.

**ai-mcp-proxy**: A request declaring a protocol revision Kong does not serve is now answered with HTTP 400 and JSON-RPC error `-32022`, listing the revisions Kong serves, instead of being served silently at a different revision.
**ai-mcp-proxy/ai-a2a-proxy**: Fixed an issue where the `mcp_server_id` and `agent_id` fields were missing from the AI analytics telemetry payload unless the plugin was scoped to a gateway service.
**ai-mcp-proxy**: Fixed an issue where AWS request signing did not read file-backed request bodies within the configured size limit.

**ai-mcp-proxy**: W3C trace context sent in `params._meta` (`traceparent`, `tracestate`, `baggage`) now reaches the upstream as headers on the request Kong actually sends, in every mode. A value containing a control character is dropped instead of being written to a header.
**ai-proxy-advanced**: Added video token metrics to the usage token details.

**ai-proxy-advanced**: Fixed an issue where a Gemini response with JSON `null` token counts in `usageMetadata` caused an HTTP 500 on non-streaming chat requests and an empty HTTP 200 response on streaming chat requests.
**ai-proxy-advanced**: Fixed an issue where adapted Anthropic responses omitted cache and reasoning usage details.
**ai-proxy-advanced**: Fixed an issue where Claude Sonnet 5 and Opus 5 rejected OpenAI-format reasoning requests on Bedrock due to an unsupported thinking.type value.
**ai-proxy-advanced**: Fixed an issue where provider-reported reasoning-token details were not correctly reported.
**ai-proxy-advanced**: Fixed an issue where some providers would not properly  respect the `stream_options: include_usage` flag, and return out-of-order SSE  stream end frames.
**ai-proxy-advanced**: Fixed an issue where xAI reasoning tokens were not folded into completion_tokens, breaking the OpenAI usage identity.
**ai-proxy-advanced**: Fixed an issue where the consistent-hashing balancer routed requests with the same hash_on_header value to different targets when multiple workers were running.

**ai-proxy-advanced**: Fixed empty and statistics-only SSE streams. Empty Anthropic responses no longer emit an unmatched `content_block_stop`, and `log_statistics`-only streams now track streamed response length for completion-token estimation.
**ai-proxy-advanced**: Fixed multipart video generation requests to OpenAI-compatible providers leaking internal multipart metadata into JSON upstream bodies, which caused the requests to fail.
**ai-proxy**: Fixed an issue where parallel tool call results were sent to Bedrock in the wrong order, causing a 400 "Expected toolResult blocks" error.
**ai-sanitizer**: Fixed an issue where ai-sanitizer returned 500 status code when the provider was using another model, such as a `claude-*` model served by the `gemini` provider on Vertex AI.

**ai-semantic-prompt-guard**, **ai-semantic-response-guard**, **ai-proxy-advanced**, **ai-semantic-cache**: Fixed vector database indexes and cached embedding records being left behind when a plugin instance was deleted.

**datakit**: Fixed an issue where the `exit` node sent a string body without a correct `Content-Type`. It now uses the content type that the source node declares, for example `application/xml` for `json_to_xml` output, and defaults to `application/octet-stream` in the request phase.

**DataKit**: Fixed the body handling of the `exit` and `service_request` nodes when the body input is a JSON null. The nodes sent the internal Lua value as the string "userdata: NULL". The `exit` node now sends no body. The `service_request` node now keeps the upstream request body.

Fixed an issue where an in-flight request that completed after its
upstream target became unavailable could restore the target to the
latency balancer and route subsequent requests to it.

Fixed an issue where `custom_validator` in schema definitions forwarded the
enclosing schema as a second argument. This changed the call signature and
could affect custom validators that declare more than one parameter. The
single-argument call signature is restored.
Fixed an issue where older data planes stopped receiving configuration updates when sync v2 was unavailable by restoring automatic sync v1 fallback.
Fixed an issue where paginated full sync could keep stale pending foreign-key references across a failed resume, causing spurious validation failures.
Fixed an issue where self-managed control planes rejected updates to a streamed plugin's handler while the plugin was referenced by a plugin instance.
Fixed an issue where streamed custom plugins were not recognized when configured in the `ordering` field of `plugins` on Data Planes.
Fixed an issue where the priority field of a cloned plugin could not be updated while it was still referenced by plugin instances.

Fixed an issue where updates to a streamed plugin's definition (e.g. `handler`), or to a cloned plugin's definition (e.g. `priority`), were not applied on data planes when no referencing plugin instances changed. The data plane now rebuilds its plugins iterator so the updated definition takes effect, instead of continuing to execute the previous version.

**jwt**: Fixed an issue where the plugin failed to decode standard Base64
secrets that contained `+` or `/` when `config.secret_is_base64` was enabled.

**kafka-consume**, **confluent-consume**: Fixed an issue where the consumer group subscription
declared protocol version 1 but carried the version 0 layout, so a topic-rewriting proxy rejected it.
**oas-validation**: Fixed an issue where the OAS specification cache failed to distinguish between different values of `api_spec_encoded` for the same specification content.

**prometheus**, **opentelemetry**: Fixed an issue where prompt-cache token usage was missing
from observability: added per-TTL cache-write token types (e.g. `cache_write_1h_tokens`,
`cache_write_5m_tokens`) to the Prometheus `ai_llm_tokens_total` and OpenTelemetry
`gen_ai.client.token.usage` metrics, and `gen_ai.usage.cache_creation.input_tokens` /
`gen_ai.usage.cache_read.input_tokens` to OpenTelemetry traces and access logs.
Improved the configuration synchronization latency when incremental sync enabled under some circumstances.

**AI Gateway**: The FIPS artifact serves an explicit TLS 1.2 cipher list: four
ECDHE suites with AES-GCM. It replaces the OpenSSL FIPS alias, which resolves
to 28 suites and also admits static RSA key transport and SSLv3-era suites. A
deployment moving from the retired `kong-ai-gateway-fips` package that relies
on one of the dropped suites must set `ssl_cipher_suite = custom` and
`ssl_ciphers`. TLS 1.3 ciphersuites are unaffected; the global OpenSSL FIPS
configuration sets those.

**AI Gateway**: The FIPS artifacts are renamed to state their certification
level. The `kong-ai-gateway-fips` package becomes
`kong-ai-gateway-fips-140-3` and the `<version>-<distro>-fips` image becomes
`<version>-<distro>-fips-140-3`. The new package replaces the old one, so an
installed FIPS deployment upgrades in place, but pinned package names and
image tags must be updated.
**openid-connect**: KONG_FIPS=on no longer generates default EdDSA JWKS keys. Use an RSA-PSS or NIST-curve ECDSA key instead.

Bumped kong-pgmoon from 2.3.4.0 to 2.3.5.0, which fixes SCRAM channel
binding failing to connect to a PostgreSQL server whose certificate is
signed with SHA-512.
Bumped lua-resty-jq from 0.2.0 to 0.2.2.
Bumped lua-resty-simdjson from 1.2.0 to 1.3.1 (updates simdjson to 4.6.11).
Bumped OpenSSL FIPS provider from 3.0.9 to 3.1.2 for FIPS 140-3 validation

Added a Distroless Docker image variant for Kong AI Gateway. The Distroless
image ships only the gateway binary and its runtime dependencies. It has no
shell, no package manager and no general-purpose userland.

Added a FIPS 140-3 variant of the Kong AI Gateway Distroless image, published
as `<version>-distroless-fips-140-3` for amd64.
Added a FIPS-compliant variant of the distroless image.
Added a new Metrics PDK (`kong.metrics`) that enables custom plugins to define and record metrics, with initial support integrated into the `opentelemetry` plugin.
**ai-mcp-proxy**: Added PDK support for effective requests, original request metadata in `log`, and pre-finalization response status and headers in `body_filter`.

**ai-mcp-proxy**: Added Token Vault support to resolve upstream credentials, allowing
the exchange and forwarding of short-lived credentials instead of static ones.
**ai-plugins**: Introduced a new filter execution ordering system so that the shared filters in AI plugins could be re-ordered. This helps bring more flexibility to the execution.

**ai-prompt-compressor**: Added a `headroom` compression provider, selected with the new
`config.provider` field. This is the stateful Headroom mode: the sidecar keeps the
compressed conversation on its own side and indexes that state by `session_id`, which the
plugin derives per conversation.
**ai-proxy**: Added support for TypeSafe.ai Jev decision models, either hosted on TypeSafe or a third-party (via custom upstream URL).
**AI Proxy**: Added the ability to choose whether to output OpenTelemetry span attributes and statistics  in OpenInference format, or the previous OpenLLMetry format.
**ai-proxy-advanced**: Added a `passthrough` route type that forwards the client's request path and body and the upstream response bytes unchanged, while still applying provider authentication.
**ai-proxy-advanced**: Added support for the OpenAI and Anthropic Skills API, with the client and the upstream provider using the same format (OpenAI-to-OpenAI, Anthropic-to-Anthropic).

**ai-rate-limiting-advanced**: Added `credential` and `service` match types to policies, so a policy can filter on or partition by the authenticated credential ID, and on the service ID or (with `key: name`) the service name.

**Analytics**: Added the W3C trace context headers (`traceparent`, `tracestate`) and, for Bedrock, SageMaker, and Vertex AI (Gemini), the inference provider's region (`ai[].meta.provider_region`) to the request payload.
Enabled TLS 1.3 for the FIPS cipher suite and configured FIPS builds to use AES-based TLS 1.3 ciphersuites.
**opentelemetry**: Added the `client_certificate` config option, so users can present a certificate entity as the mTLS client certificate when an OTLP endpoint uses HTTPS.

Required identical AI Gateway versions on control planes and data planes before
allowing full or incremental configuration synchronization. Data planes with
missing versions or different patch or prerelease versions were rejected.
**ACME**: Fixed an issue where an expired `fail_backoff` key would keep blocking certificate issuance. Retries are now rejected only while the backoff timestamp is still in the future.
**ai-a2a-proxy**: Fixed an issue where `proxy_config` was not applied to the final A2A upstream request.
**ai-a2a-proxy**: Rejected `auth.provider: token_vault` at config validation time, since this plugin only implements `aws_iam` auth.
**AI Analytics**: Fixed an issue where `ai.model_id` were absent in Analytics
**ai-aws-guardrails**: Fixed handling of OpenAI-compatible multimodal requests with image content.

**AI Gateway**: Fixed the RPM `Obsoletes` metadata of the AI Gateway packages.
`kong-ai-gateway` and `kong-ai-gateway-fips-140-3` are parallel builds, not
successors of each other, so they now obsolete each other only below the
version being built. Without the bound an installed `kong-ai-gateway` had two
mutually conflicting successors and `dnf upgrade` could not resolve an
upgrade. The retired `kong-ai-gateway-fips` keeps a single unversioned
successor, `kong-ai-gateway-fips-140-3`, so an existing FIPS deployment
upgrades in place. The deb packages do not change.
**ai-mcp-proxy**: Fixed an issue where setting `server.tag` in conversion-listener mode returned an empty tool list.
**ai-mcp-proxy**: Fixed an issue where modern MCP mirroring headers were forwarded to legacy upstream servers.
**ai-mcp-proxy**: Fixed an issue where plugins before ai-mcp-proxy were run twice in conversion-listener mode.

**ai-prompt-compressor**: Fixed an issue where, on routes where the client and the upstream use the same format, the compressor sent the original request instead of the one modified by ai-sanitizer, masking guardrails, ai-rag-injector or ai-request-transformer.
**ai-proxy-advanced**: Added prompt cache control mappings across OpenAI, Anthropic, and Amazon Bedrock chat formats.
**ai-proxy-advanced**: Fixed a path-duplication bug on Anthropic restful routes (`llm/v1/batches`, `llm/v1/skills`) when the model used a custom `upstream_url`.
**ai-proxy-advanced**: Fixed an issue where Gemini image generation misattributed modality tokens and omitted cache usage in responses and AI logs.
**ai-proxy-advanced**: Fixed an issue where gen_ai.request.max_tokens attribute was missing from OpenTelemetry and debug-session spans.
**ai-proxy-advanced**: Fixed an issue where Anthropic-compatible streaming providers like Baseten reporting prompt usage only in `message_delta` lost prompt and cached tokens.
**ai-proxy-advanced**: Fixed an issue where Anthropic `thinking.type = "disabled"` was overridden by `output_config.effort` during cross-format conversion, keeping reasoning enabled.

**ai-proxy-advanced**: Fixed an issue where an Anthropic `thinking` block (`adaptive`, `enabled`, or
`disabled`) was always converted into a `reasoning_effort` request parameter and forwarded to the
target model, even when that model did not support reasoning. OpenAI, Mistral, and Cohere targets
without reasoning support now have the gateway-derived value omitted, while an explicit
`reasoning_effort` sent by the client is still forwarded as before.
**ai-proxy-advanced**: Fixed an issue where Bedrock and SageMaker assume-role credentials were not prewarmed and could trigger STS calls during balancer-phase retries.
**ai-proxy-advanced**: Fixed an issue where the consistent-hashing balancer routed requests with the same hash_on_header value to different targets when multiple workers were running.
**ai-proxy-advanced**: Fixed an issue where repeated cumulative usage in streaming responses inflated token counts.
**ai-proxy-advanced**: Fixed an issue where xAI reasoning tokens were not folded when visible completion tokens exceeded reasoning tokens.
**ai-proxy-advanced**: Fixed an issue where Anthropic streaming responses and Bedrock native-format responses did not report web search and web fetch tool usage counts in observability metrics.

**ai-proxy-advanced**: Fixed an issue where Anthropic `output_config.effort` was ignored during cross-format conversion (including Bedrock `additionalModelRequestFields`), and added support for preserving `max` effort.
**ai-response-transformer**: Fixed an issue where a chained upstream's raw, provider-native response was sent to introspection and returned to clients unnormalized.
**ai-sanitizer**: Fixed an issue where ai-sanitizer only sanitized the first Gemini response candidate, leaving additional candidates unsanitized when candidateCount was greater than one.
**ai-sanitizer**: Fixed an issue where ai-sanitizer failed to sanitize Cohere requests that contained multimodal message content, such as image blocks alongside text.
**Analytics**: splunk reports now carry `ai_a2a_reqs` and `ai_total_reqs` fields, counting A2A requests and all AI Gateway traffic (inference, MCP, and A2A) respectively.

**Balancer**: Fixed an issue where a plugin could not override the upstream
target when the Gateway Service `host` was a literal IP address. The balancer
kept the IP that it derived from the Service, so the request went to the
Service host and the override was silently lost. This affected
`kong.service.set_target` and every plugin that replaces
`ngx.ctx.balancer_data.host`, for example `route-transformer-advanced` and
`canary`.

**datakit**: Fixed an issue where the `exit` node sent a string body without a correct `Content-Type`. It now uses the content type that the source node declares, for example `application/xml` for `json_to_xml` output, and defaults to `application/octet-stream` in the request phase.

Fixed an issue where a malformed JSON document could corrupt the shared JSON
decoder of a worker. Later requests that decoded valid JSON on the same worker
then failed until the node restarted. The JWT plugin returned
`Bad token; invalid JWT payload` for known-good tokens.

Fixed an issue where an in-flight request that completed after its
upstream target became unavailable could restore the target to the
latency balancer and route subsequent requests to it.

Fixed an issue where `custom_validator` in schema definitions forwarded the
enclosing schema as a second argument. This changed the call signature and
could affect custom validators that declare more than one parameter. The
single-argument call signature is restored.
Fixed an issue where older data planes stopped receiving configuration updates when sync v2 was unavailable by restoring automatic sync v1 fallback.
Fixed an issue where the `SameSite` attribute of the `Set-Cookie` header was incorrectly set to `Same-Site` by session-affinity (sticky-session) balancing.
**graphql-rate-limiting-advanced**: Fixed an issue where a longer fixed window was incorrectly marked as exhausted if a shorter window denied a request.

Hardened stale nginx PID detection to survive PID reuse. On Linux, `kong start`
now confirms a live PID actually belongs to nginx by reading `/proc/<pid>/cmdline`,
so a reused PID from an ungraceful exit no longer blocks a restart.

**jwt**: Fixed an issue where the plugin failed to decode standard Base64
secrets that contained `+` or `/` when `config.secret_is_base64` was enabled.

On shell-free (distroless) images, the pluginserver query and start commands
now expand `$KONG_PREFIX` / `${KONG_PREFIX}` from the environment and fail fast
with a clear error on an unterminated quote or `${`, instead of passing the
literal `$KONG_PREFIX` to the pluginserver or building a best-effort argv.

**opa**: Fixed an issue where Kong Gateway did not send an SNI to the OPA server. It now sends `opa_host` as the SNI when that is a hostname; with `ssl_verify = true`, the certificate must include `opa_host`.

**openid-connect**: Fixed an issue where disabling `verify_signature` gave no warning, even though it also skips signature verification for bearer tokens from clients. The plugin now logs a warning when `verify_signature` is `false` and `auth_methods` includes `bearer`. It logs a notice instead when `bearer` is not enabled.
**openid-connect**: Fixed an issue where a callback with an invalid JARM response returned a 500 error; the plugin now rejects such callbacks with a 401 authentication failure.

**opentelemetry**: Fixed an issue where metrics were rarely (or never) exported on data planes whose configuration is rebuilt more frequently than the metrics `push_interval`. The periodic metrics push timer is no longer cancelled and recreated on every configuration rebuild, so its `push_interval` countdown is preserved.
**rate-limiting-advanced**: Fixed an issue where a longer fixed window was incorrectly marked as exhausted if a shorter window denied a request.

**request-callout**: Fixed an issue where a callout that failed and then succeeded
on retry still returned the earlier failed response. The plugin now returns the
response from the successful retry.
**service-protection**: Fixed an issue where a longer fixed window was incorrectly marked as exhausted if a shorter window denied a request.

**ai-mcp-proxy**: Cached Token Vault credential exchanges using Redis to reduce
